subtitulo: Speculating about who is accountable when AI decides
descripcion: At C1, speculation is built as a chain: an observation, a graded prediction, and an explicit acknowledgement of what could prove it wrong. A flat prediction with no qualification reads as overconfident; this chain is what makes a forecast sound credible rather than guessed.

filas: Given how things have gone so far,…
…it's likely to keep drifting in that direction.
Though a lot could still change that.

ejemplos.texto: Given how things have gone so far, it's likely to keep drifting the same way.
If current trends hold, we could see a real shift within the year.
That said, a lot could still change between now and then.

notas: Likely to and bound to differ in strength: bound to reads as near-certain, likely to leaves real room for doubt.
Starting a prediction with an observation (given how things have gone) grounds it in evidence rather than a guess out of nowhere.
Closing with an acknowledged limit (a lot could still change) is what keeps a confident prediction from sounding reckless.

contraste.es: Si se mantiene la tendencia actual corresponds exactly to if current trends hold, so conditional predictions transfer. The English habit is to anchor the prediction in that observation before stating it.
contraste.de: Wenn der Trend anhält corresponds exactly to if current trends hold, and dürfte maps well onto is likely to. Conditional predictions therefore transfer directly.
contraste.it: Se l'andamento attuale continua corresponds well to if current trends continue, so conditional predictions transfer. The Italian future of probability should not be rendered with will, which sounds more certain.
contraste.fr: Si la tendance se maintient corresponds exactly to if current trends hold, so conditional predictions transfer directly.
contraste.pt: Se a tendência se mantiver uses the future subjunctive, which can lead to the calque if the trend will hold. English uses the present after if: if current trends hold.

errores: Jumping straight to a prediction without grounding it in an observation first.
Confusing likely to and bound to and overstating the confidence of a prediction.
Never acknowledging what could prove the prediction wrong.

es: *Todo apunta a que* rendered as *Everything points to that* instead of *All the signs are that*.
de: *Es ist davon auszugehen, dass* rendered as *It is to go out from that* instead of *It's safe to assume that*.
it: *Tutto lascia pensare che* rendered as *Everything lets think that* instead of *All the signs are that*.
fr: *Tout porte à croire que* rendered as *Everything carries to believe that* instead of *All the signs are that*.
pt: *Ao que tudo indica* rendered as *To what everything indicates* instead of *By all indications*.

mision.consigna: Speculate on how AI decisions at work will be regulated within ten years.
requisitos: an observation, a graded prediction, and what would prove you wrong
one explicit *That said, a lot could change*

microtareas.texto: Write three predictions about *black box* systems at different strengths.
For each, write the fact that would make you revise it.
Record 90 seconds: will people be able to *opt out*? Graded throughout.

autochequeo: Is the prediction grounded in a stated observation?
Is the confidence level (likely vs bound to) accurate to the evidence?
Is there an explicit acknowledgement of what could prove it wrong?
Does the prediction avoid sounding like a flat guess?
Would a listener sense confident guessing rather than reasoned speculation?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the speculation chain: observation, graded prediction, acknowledged uncertainty. Check whether the prediction is grounded in evidence, whether the confidence level matches it, and whether an explicit limit is stated. Do not rewrite the text.
